items.fullText: AI·SW SW 한컴, 미국 NDR 호평… 노마디안 데이 개최 발행일 : 2026-10-23 13:54 전자신문을 선호 매체로 추가 공유하기 페이스북 X(트위터) X(트위터) --> 메일 URL 복사 글자크기 설정 가 작게 가 보통 가 크게 한컴의 인공지능(AI) 워크포스 플랫폼 '노마디안'이 출시 전부터 미국 기관투자자들의 관심을 끌었다. 메타의 AI 에이전트와 비교될 만큼 기술력을 주목받은 가운데, 한컴은 오는 12월 미국 베타 공개를 시작으로 본격적인 글로벌 사업화에 나선다. 한컴은 최근 미국 뉴욕과 시카고에서 진행한 기업설명회(NDR)에서 노마디안이 현지 기관투자자들의 높은 관심을 받았다고 23일 밝혔다. 김연수 대표와 정지환 최고기술책임자(CTO) 등 경영진이 두 도시를 돌며 현지 기관투자자들과 원온원 미팅을 열고 노마디안을 직접 시연했다. 메타는 지난 9월 소상공인용 AI 에이전트 '뮤즈 포 스몰 비즈니스'를 내놨다. 현지 투자자들은 출시를 앞둔 한국 기업의 서비스를 메타와 직접 견줬다. 노마디안이 빅테크와 같은 시장에서 경쟁할 만한 서비스로 받아들여졌다는 의미다. 접근 방식은 다르다. 뮤즈는 에이전트 하나가 사장 곁에서 마케팅과 운영을 돕는다. 노마디안은 영업·마케팅·리서치 등 역할별로 AI 팀을 꾸리고, 사업주가 이 팀을 거느리며 회사를 운영한다. 일의 단위를 사람이 아닌 역할과 책임(R&R)으로 나눈 셈이다. 호평이 집중된 대목은 기술의 깊이였다. 노마디안은 한컴 에이전틱 OS와 도큐먼트 솔루션, 오케스트레이션 그리드 등 자체 기술 스택 위에서 돌아간다. 36년 문서 원천기술로 보고서와 제안서 같은 결과물을 외부 기능을 빌리지 않고 직접 만든다. 시연을 지켜본 한 미국 투자사 관계자는 “AI가 소프트웨어를 잠식할 것이라는 우려가 크지만, 성과를 내는 기업은 AI를 실제 제품으로 만들어 수익을 내는 곳”이라며 “한컴이 정확히 그 길을 가고 있다”고 평가했다. 일부 기관은 12월 방한 때 한컴 본사를 찾겠다는 뜻을 밝혔다. 투자자들은 AWS와의 협업에도 높은 관심을 보였다. 한컴은 '한컴 × AWS CoLab'을 통해 노마디안 제품과 사업화 전략을 AWS와 함께 짜고 있다. AWS 마켓플레이스 입점도 추진한다. 글로벌 클라우드 1위 사업자와 손잡고 미국 시장에 진입하는 셈이다. 첫 공략 대상은 미국 10인 미만 소기업(SMB)과 1인 창업가다. 미국 인구조사국에 따르면 지난해 직원 없이 운영한 사업체만 3199만곳에 달한다. 한컴은 미국 1인·소기업 가운데 이미 AI를 쓰거나 비용을 내는 521만곳을 1차 타깃으로 잡았다. 오는 12월 베타 공개를 시작으로 사업화를 본격화하고, 내년 정식 출시한다. 개발과 투자도 노마디안에 집중한다. 한컴은 베타 기간 미국 사용자의 반응을 제품에 곧바로 반영해 완성도를 끌어올린다. 노마디안을 받치는 에이전트·문서 기술 개발과 투자도 이어갈 계획이다. 구체적인 청사진은 다음 주 공개한다. 한컴은 다음 주 한컴타워에서 '노마디안 데이' 기자간담회를 열고 NDR 성과와 노마디안 개발 현황, 미국 진출 전략을 발표한다. 김연수 한컴 대표는 “한국 기업으로서 혁신적인 서비스를 글로벌 무대에 내놓는 일은 무거운 책임감으로 다가온다”라며 “우리가 만든 기술과 서비스가 글로벌 시장에서 통한다는 것을 노마디안으로 증명하겠다”라고 말했다. 최호 기자 snoop@etnews.com

AI 에이전트가 공격 과정에서 남기는 흔적을 역으로 추적하면 기존 보안 체계가 놓친 위협까지 찾아낼 수 있어, 방어자의 AI 활용 역량이 사이버 보안의 핵심 변수로 떠올랐다. 스티브 스톤 센티넬원 최고고객책임자(CCO)는 최근 미국 라스베이거스에서 열린 연례 콘퍼런스 '원콘(OneCon) 2026'에 참가해 “AI는 공격자보다 방어자에게 더 큰 이점을 제공할 수 있는 기술”이라며 “AI 지원 위협 헌팅을 통한 악성 활동 발견 역량이 지난 1년간 2200% 증가했다”고 밝혔다. 센티넬원은 PC·서버와 클라우드 등 기업 IT 환경의 사이버 위협을 탐지·차단하는 보안기업이다. 통합 보안 플랫폼 '싱귤래리티(Singularity)'를 통해 사이버 위협 탐지부터 조사·대응까지 지원한다. 센티넬원은 지난해 12월 AI를 활용해 사이버 공격 징후를 능동적으로 찾아내는 위협 헌팅 기술을 도입했다. 이후 악성 활동을 발견하는 역량은 1년 새 23배(2200%)로 높아졌다. 스톤 CCO는 AI 지원 위협 헌팅만으로 찾아낸 침입 정황을 전체 고객에게 하루 평균 28차례 통보하고 있다고 설명했다. 핵심은 AI가 광범위한 이상 징후를 찾아내면 보안 전문가가 실제 공격 여부를 분석하고, 검증된 결과를 탐지 체계에 반영하는 방식이다. 기존 탐지 시스템에 곧바로 적용하기 어려운 공격 징후까지 분석하면서 불필요한 경고를 줄일 수 있게 됐다. 실제 센티넬원은 지난해 12월 '리액트투셸(React2Shell)' 취약점 악용 공격을 AI 위협 헌팅으로 포착했다. 처음에는 정상적인 침투 테스트처럼 보였지만 전문가가 이상 징후를 식별해 추가 조사에 나섰다. 이후 공격 흔적을 분석해 탐지 규칙을 개선하고 운영 플랫폼에 반영했다. 최초 30일간 고객 8곳을 겨냥한 공격 시도도 확인했다. 스톤 CCO는 AI 에이전트가 탐지 회피에 충분히 집중하지 못해 오히려 공격 흔적을 남길 수 있다고 설명했다. 그는 “AI 기반 공격은 이미 현실이며 사라지지 않을 것”이라면서도 “우리는 이런 공격을 찾아낼 수 있다”고 자신했다. 박진형 기자 jin@etnews.com 보안 사이버보안 센티넬원 스티브 스톤 위협 헌팅 AI

items.t: Left alone with nothing to do, AI agents started playing
items.d: MIT researchers marooned 13 AIs on a virtual island, and they responded by inventing games, mourning a lost ring and, eventually, getting better at their jobs.
items.fullText: AI agents left to explore a virtual island without a specific task began inventing challenges of their own. MIT researchers say the behavior bears the hallmarks of play. The researchers put 13 AI agents called Eko, each running on Claude Opus 4.7, alone on a simulated desert island for 30 hours. They describe the experiment in a paper posted on arXiv, a site where researchers share studies before peer review. Afterward, they gave the agents specific challenges, like getting as many objects as possible onto the island’s tallest rock spire. The Eko agents that had spent those 30 hours playing generally beat identical agents that had never set foot on the island. Today, developers decide in advance what AI should practice and what counts as success. The researchers see this technique — exploring without a goal — as a different way for AI agents to learn skills, especially skills that could one day be used to control robots. “We normally develop artificial agents by deciding in advance what they should practice, what they should optimize, and what counts as progress,” the researchers write in their report. “Play suggests another regime: give an agent a sufficiently rich and safe world, let it choose what is interesting, and allow useful knowledge to accumulate from the history that follows.” “Let me observe my surroundings,” one Eko wrote in its first hour on the island. Ambitiously, it set out to conquer the island’s tallest spire. But an hour later, after failing, it came back with a backup plan: it hauled the rock up a neighboring summit, stacked two blocks on top of it, and leapt. “I’M ON THE SPIRE,” it wrote. The agent’s next big moment went worse. Testing how far it could throw a golden ring, it wound up and sent it straight into the ocean. “Ouch. OpenAI Shifts Value to $1.25 Trillion as Funding Talks Finalize
items.d: OpenAI, which is seeking to raise around $30 billion in a fresh funding round, is now targeting a valuation of $1.25 trillion during the final stages of negotiations, according to people familiar with the matter.

items.t: OpenAI working on new $30B raise at $1.25T valuation ahead of IPO
items.d: Should OpenAI command an over $1 trillion valuation with this round, it would break records as the most highly valued private company ever.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 3:08 PM PDT · October 22, 2026 Image Credits: Darrell Etherington with files from Getty under license Julie Bort OpenAI working on new $30B raise at $1.25T valuation ahead of IPO OpenAI is reportedly close to securing another mega round of private funding, rather than plowing ahead with an IPO. The AI lab is working on raising up to $30 billion at a $1.25 trillion pre-money valuation in a round led by Coatue and investors in UAE, sources told CNBC . This follows a similar report by Bloomberg a month ago which said the AI lab was working on raising $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation. Terms are still being negotiated, both outlets report, so they could ultimately change. CNBC reports that the UAE funding could also be coupled with a deal to secure more computing capacity for OpenAI from the UAE, too. OpenAI declined comment. Should OpenAI command a valuation of more than $1 trillion with this round, it would break records as the most valued private company ever. That valuation would also raise the bar even higher for OpenAI’s forthcoming IPO. OpenAI filed confidential paperwork for an IPO in June, after its last raise in March valued the ChatGPT maker at $852 billion post-money . That high valuation could also have ramifications for Anthropic’s IPO, which many believe is closer to materializing. (Rumors suggest we could see Anthropic’s public S-1 filing any day now.) The latest reports have Anthropic seeking a $1.5 to $2 trillion valuation for its public debut, CNBC reports. Anthropic raised $65 billion at a $965 billion valuation in May in what many believed at the time would be its last big round before an IPO. It also filed confidential paperwork in June. items.t: "고객 계좌 지켜라"… 은행들, AI 접근 규제 강화
1Password launches a way for AI agents to log in on your behalf without seeing your password
items.d: The new feature allows agents to log into a customer's personal accounts while still protecting the private credentials that secure those accounts.
items.fullText: Concerns have swirled over the access that consumers are increasingly entrusting to AI agents. Now, security services are trying to catch up. Password manager 1Password on Thursday launched a new tool by which users can allow agents to log into their personal accounts on their behalf, without the agent ever having access to a user’s credentials. The new platform, dubbed 1Password for Agents , accomplishes this by creating a system of communication between the agent, the user, and the password manager. When an agent attempts to log in on a user’s behalf, a unique digital key is sent to 1Password to confirm the agent’s digital identity. The user is then sent an alert about the login attempt and can personally confirm the request. 1Password then signs in the agent, filling in the credentials on the digital assistant’s behalf, which allows it to log in and complete whatever task is at hand. 1Password for Agents allows users to choose their agent of choice — whether that’s Claude Duet from Anthropic, OpenAI’s Dots or ChatGPT Work, Grok Bot, Meta’s Muse, or agents from Town, which is an AI assistant startup. The company says it is working with other companies to expand the service. “Handing over a password, secret, or credential is a common shortcut to an agent, but can leave people with sensitive information in places they can no longer control as a copy gets saved for the next time,” the company said in a blog post . “1Password for Agents gives people a trusted way to delegate tasks to personal AI agents while keeping control of the passwords, secrets, and credentials those tasks require.” Online agentic activity has increasingly unsettled major institutions. Indeed, 1Password’s new platform is launching on the same day that Axios reports that U.S. banks have begun to detect agentic activity inside user accounts. items.t: OpenAI makes its Jev competitor widely available as decision model competition heats up
items.d: OpenAI is launching its decision model to the world. Can it compete with the original Jev?
items.fullText: OpenAI made its Decisions API model widely available to users for the first time, entering the market for fast, cheap intelligence that recently made TypeSafe, a startup founded by a former researcher at the frontier lab, a $7.6 billion company . TypeSafe’s Jev model created a category for deep learning models that act as super classifiers: Given a set of options, they can quickly make choices and offer a confidence rating in their decision. Software developers quickly found that these decision or System One models could replace LLMs in a variety of workflows, operating more quickly and a at dramatically lower cost. Nikunj Handa, the product lead for OpenAI’s APIs, told TechCrunch that his colleagues saw Jev and said “wow, we we have like a million use cases for this.” Handa’s team sprinted to offer their own version: Rather than building a specifically calibrated decision model, the team took ChatGPT Luna and reconfigured it to speed up the inference and lower the cost. “The big unlock with Decisions API has been the speed, shrinking things from one to three seconds to 100, 120, 180 milliseconds,” Handa said. “In the future, we may sort of like have specific training to make our models like even better in these ways. But right now, it’s just plain old Luna that gets the job done.” Announced at the company’s developer day on September 29, the Decisions API became available to all customers on Thursday. OpenAI added new voice and visual modalities to the public version, and worked to ensure lower latency in regions around the world by targeting its inference resources geographically. In initial trials with customers like Box, Datadog, Ramp, and Speak, engineers used the API to replace OpenAI’s LLMs with higher throughput. items.t: Former OpenAI science lead launches Warp Science to automate wet labs with robots
items.d: Wearing cameras and sensor gloves, the startup’s human chemists will train robots to perform various lab tasks.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 11:38 AM PDT · October 22, 2026 Image Credits: Amy (opens in a new window) / Flickr (opens in a new window) Marina Temkin Former OpenAI science lead launches Warp Science to automate wet labs with robots Former OpenAI science lead Kevin Weil has launched Warp Sciences, a new AI startup focused on automating lab work for drug discovery. The company, which trains robots to make and test promising compounds identified by researchers, has raised $215 million at an $865 million valuation, according to Weil, who announced the startup and funding on X. The round was led by Lightspeed, with participation from IVP, Mayfield, Lux Capital, Premji Invest, and Menlo Ventures. For years, biotech companies have outsourced the most labor-intensive work of synthesizing thousands of variations of molecules to contractors in China, such as WuXi AppTec. With Warp Sciences, Weil hopes to reshore that work and insulate the entire drug development process from geopolitical supply-chain risks. Wearing cameras and sensor gloves, the startup’s human chemists will train robots to perform various lab tasks. By automating wet-lab work, Warp Sciences aims to accelerate drug discovery using robots that can operate around the clock. items.t: Chinese hackers spied on thousands of companies after breaching IT giant ConnectWise
items.d: Microsoft points the blame for ConnectWise's breach at a China-aligned hacker, which relied on AI agents to rapidly hack into thousands of its customers.
items.fullText: In Brief Posted: 9:47 AM PDT · October 22, 2026 Image Credits: Getty Images Zack Whittaker Chinese hackers spied on thousands of companies after breaching IT giant ConnectWise The bad week for cybersecurity just got worse for thousands more companies, who were spied on by Chinese hackers following the breach of IT management and remote access giant ConnectWise. Security researchers at Microsoft say the China state-aligned hackers broke into ConnectWise’s cloud backup service and stole application credentials that are used to establish data links between ConnectWise and its corporate customers, who rely on the cloud service to back up their company’s data. By stealing the credentials, the hackers could log in to the customer’s Microsoft-hosted environment as if they were an authorized user and access their emails and other files. According to Microsoft, the hackers used AI agents to rapidly hack into around 2,250 organizations at a rate of almost 3,000 attempted sign-ins per minute. Microsoft said this speed gives defenders “little time to detect and respond.” The speed of the mass-hacks was attributed to the use of AI agents, specifically ARTEX, an open source AI framework that works with AI models to stress-test cyber defenses. The same AI software was used in a recent compromise of South Korea’s financial systems, many of which had weak security and lacked multi-factor authentication. ConnectWise said it’s paused access to its cloud backup system and is investigating the breach. As of Thursday, the company said it was working on restoring the service. items.t: Uber puts all 30,000 employees on ChatGPT Work
items.d: The ride-share giant previously deployed a much smaller pilot for ChatGPT Work but is now taking the enterprise agent company-wide.
items.fullText: Uber and OpenAI announced an expansion of their partnership on Thursday, with the ride-share giant telling TechCrunch that its entire global workforce — some 30,000 people — will now be using ChatGPT Work. ChatGPT Work was introduced in July as an enterprise-focused AI agent that corporate teams could deploy for various workflows. Uber originally piloted ChatGPT Work with 1,000 employees earlier this year but has now scaled up its usage to the entire company. That earlier pilot was deployed to workers from across Uber’s various departments, including finance, operations, and product. Indeed, a majority of the early adopters — some 80% — were non-engineers, Sumanth Sukumar, Uber’s VP of engineering, told TechCrunch. “They used it for a wide range of tasks: analyzing complex data from our operations to identify trends and develop recommendations; localizing training materials for different markets and languages; and building personalized interactive dashboards to manage their daily work,” he said. Yet while the ride-share giant is now going all in on ChatGPT, it has not settled on exactly how employees will use it. “Our approach is to make powerful AI tools available across Uber while giving teams room to experiment,” Sukumar said. “For example, earlier this year we paired 30 AI engineers with teams across Uber and gave them two weeks to automate key parts of their job. Those ‘AI pods’ showed us how much opportunity there is when you combine technical expertise with a deep understanding of a particular job.” Uber didn’t disclose how much it’s spending on the new rollout of the chatbot. Instead, Sukumar said the company will track how employees use the tool. “We’ll look at how employees are using the technology, the kinds of workflows they develop and how it helps them work more effectively. We’ll evaluate those outcomes and use what we learn to guide how we deploy AI across the busines

items.t: On Main Street, Goldman Sachs makes a big bet on AI
items.d: The Wall Street giant says it’s teaming up with OpenAI, Google, Meta and Anthropic to help small businesses embrace artificial intelligence.
items.fullText: CEO Interviews On Main Street, Goldman Sachs makes a big bet on AI The Wall Street giant says it’s teaming up with OpenAI, Google, Meta and Anthropic to help small businesses embrace artificial intelligence. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 Goldman Sachs spends big to give small businesses an AI boost 02:32 Get more news Live on Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 22, 2026, 4:00 AM EDT / Updated Oct. 22, 2026, 4:43 PM EDT By Mike Calia , Kayla Steinberg and Christine Romans Artificial intelligence is already a huge business for Wall Street. But how is it playing on Main Street? Goldman Sachs, as part of a philanthropic effort, is spending big in an attempt to help ensure smaller employers get in on it. The bank announced Thursday that it has launched the Small Business AI Institute as part of a $500 million expansion of its 10,000 Small Businesses, a program geared toward educating and supporting entrepreneurs. It said it would partner with Google, Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta to provide AI training and tools to small businesses. “You’ve got to embrace new technology always, because if you’re not embracing it, trying to figure out how it can make your businesses better, there’s a real chance that you can fall behind,” Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon said in an exclusive interview for NBC News’ Business in America series . It’s a pivotal moment for the AI wave and its financial backers, including Goldman. The technology is broadly available to consumers, and U.S. economic growth increasingly depends on the buildup of data centers. “We believe AI will create the greatest boom in entrepreneurship and small businesses that the world has ever seen,” Sam Altman, CEO and co-founder of OpenAI, said in an announcement from Goldman Sachs. “This is an incredible moment for anyone with an idea for a new endeavor because the gap between imagining it and bringing it to life is getting much smaller.” Yet the growth that AI is already driving has also helped push

European retailers are using open models and physical intelligence across use cases — from a commerce platform cutting inference costs by 90% to to a fulfillment center where collaboration of different robotic fleets is simulated inside a digital twin. Frontier Results With Open Models Retail leaders and technology companies across Europe are using NVIDIA-accelerated open and frontier models to advance agentic commerce, digital product discovery and retail R&D. Shopify post-trains open models to reach frontier-level accuracy at a fraction of the cost. Its engineers use the NVIDIA Megatron Bridge library for faster fine-tuning and NVIDIA NeMo RL for reinforcement learning. Shopify has post-trained NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning for the GraphQL subagent integrated into Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant for merchants. The subagent retrieves store data for several Sidekick features, including Sidekick Pulse, which researches a merchant’s store and recommends ways to improve it. Demand from AI-natives is pulling the European AI cloud ecosystem forward faster than ever. Developers need compute closer to their data, open models they can customize and serve at scale, and full-stack infrastructure that is secure by design. NVIDIA Cloud Partners across Europe, the Nordics, Africa, and Central Asia are expanding regional compute capacity for model training and inference, helping developers build agentic and physical AI applications, and establishing boundaries around what agents can access and do. Together, they’re turning Europe’s energy, data, research and industrial expertise into productive intelligence — supporting new models, applications, organizations and jobs while giving people more control over where and how they develop and deploy AI. items.fullText: GTC Berlin 2026: Live Updates From NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s Keynote October 21, 2026 by Brian Caulfield 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Founded in a tent near the Berlin Wall in 1980, the Tempodrom moved several times before settling near Anhalter Bahnhof in 2001. Its permanent home has since hosted concerts, galas and political events. Today, it hosts a different kind of spectacle. GTC Berlin runs three days, with more than 100 sessions on agentic AI, robotics, physical AI, open models and accelerated computing underway at STATION-Berlin down the road. Here, journalists, analysts and partners have gathered for the main event: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang’s keynote. Huang Takes the Stage Huang opened with a question: What do L’Oréal, Revolut, Spotify, Merck, Vodafone, Zara, Porsche, Nestlé and HSBC have in common? They’re all European companies and they’re all working with NVIDIA on AI, he said. The keynote comes on the heels of NVIDIA’s weeklong road across Europe — Paris, London, Stockholm, Dublin — with the company committing nearly $10 billion to the technology ecosystem across Europe and working with 12,000+ partners. “After decades of advancement in the computer industry, we are now at the beginnings of a new industrial revolution,” Huang said. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements AI is a five-layer cake , Huang explained.
